solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dreadful booze changes tourist's colour?

definitions.meaning: slang for cheap, harsh spirits that taste as if they could strip varnish
read as two words, PAINTS (colours) and TRIPPER (a day tourist): one who colours a holidaymaker

explanation.surface: Rough local liquor turns a holidaymaker's face a different shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the phrase after the S and it reads 'paints tripper', a TRIPPER being a British day-tourist.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for rough, harsh alcohol is the name of the solvent used to remove old coatings from woodwork.

clue.text: A sweet location — chapel should be moved here

indicators.note: moving the letters around puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A pleasant site where a church building ought to be relocated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' is only a link; the anagram uses every letter of LOCATION and CHAPEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark confectionery without milk is an example of a sweet treat.

clue.text: Small map — it covers most of the cardinal points

indicators.note: the two letters wrap round the others
all but the last letter of the points

parts.note: N, S, E and W are the four compass points

explanation.surface: A small map spread over most of the compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small subsidiary map placed within the border of a larger one.

clue.text: Flickering illumination shows something wrong about church land mostly

indicators.note: the wrong goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to light is to land or come down, as a bird alights

explanation.surface: A legal wrong over church land, revealed by a wavering light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' is a verb here, as a bird alights; 'mostly' drops its final letter, and 'about' sets the legal wrong around church plus that remnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from a burning brand or flaming torch flickers, a wavering form of illumination.

clue.text: Credible catch, stored in box

indicators.note: the catch is placed inside

parts.note: the box is slang for television, the tele
to nab is to catch or seize

explanation.surface: A believable catch kept in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable position is one that can be defended, so believable or plausible.

clue.text: Winter spectacular — costs twice reduced at the beginning (and how!)

indicators.note: the front is cut by one letter two times

parts.note: prices are costs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A seasonal extravaganza whose ticket costs were cut twice right away, and how!
explanation.definitionFit: A skating show on a rink is a cold-season extravaganza, an entertainment on frozen ground.

clue.text: Place's opening or closing? Opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the closing of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether a place is opening or closing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place's opening or closing' is read literally: P, then OR, then E, the place's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny holes in the skin are minute openings, so this is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Discharge that damages body during uproar

indicators.note: the body comes inside the uproar

parts.note: a riot is a noisy uproar
flesh is the body

explanation.surface: A discharge that harms the body during a riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Firing a gun is a discharge, and a bullet from it harms whatever it hits.

clue.text: Pastoral literary production has phrase involved with 'hard soil'

indicators.note: something involved is twisted together, so the letters become tangled

explanation.surface: A rural literary work with a phrase about 'hard soil'.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is a rural English county; Housman's 1896 poem cycle is named after a young man from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A E Housman's collection of poems about rustic English life is a pastoral work of literature.

clue.text: Guarantee a variety of users will receive a new computer at the outset

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the following pieces
a variety is a different form, so the letters of users appear in another order
the outset of computer is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A sales pitch promising that software users will each get a new computer from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a variety of' reads as 'several', but 'variety of' is the anagram signal and the first 'a' is a letter; 'will receive' puts the second A, new and the computer's initial inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An assurance is a pledge or promise, the same thing as a guarantee given to someone.

clue.text: Red-haired person's hair coming back to us

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is a red-haired person

indicators.note: the word for hair is read backwards in this across entry

parts.note: fur is the hair of an animal

explanation.surface: A redhead's hair returning to the family, as if a lock came back to us.
explanation.walkthrough: Rufus is Latin for red, and was the nickname of William II of England for his ruddy complexion.
explanation.definitionFit: The name or nickname comes from the Latin adjective for reddish, given to a ginger-haired man.

clue.text: Avoiding new developments, expending energy to make mark on wood?

indicators.note: spending something means using it up, so the energy letter goes

parts.note: shunning modern gadgets means having no tech
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A traditionalist carpenter refuses modern tools and works by hand to leave a cut in timber.
explanation.walkthrough: NO TECH loses its E. The question mark flags that a nick or cut is only one example of a mark on wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A V-shaped nick cut into timber is a typical incision made with a knife or saw.

clue.text: Scientist passing oxygen and hydrogen through bromine

indicators.note: one element is sent into another, so these letters go inside
going through something means being within it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: Br is the chemical symbol for bromine
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A chemist bubbling gases through a liquid element in a laboratory experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was the Danish physicist who modelled the atom, a famous Nobel-winning scientist.

clue.text: Fruit-tree — perfect example for trimming

indicators.note: trimming cuts off an end, so the last letter of the example goes

parts.note: a pearl is a prized, flawless specimen of something

explanation.surface: A gardener choosing an ideal specimen tree to prune.
explanation.definitionFit: This orchard tree bears the pear-shaped fruit, and the name serves for both the plant and its produce.

clue.text: Substantial reminder regarding legal action not clearly indicated

parts.note: a prod is a nudge to remind someone

indicators.note: the second word is taken out of the first

parts.note: litigious means concerned with lawsuits
something lit up is clearly shown

explanation.surface: A firm reminder about a lawsuit that had not been clearly signposted.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigious means enormous in size or extent, so a near synonym of large or substantial.

clue.text: Image seen in Tube shows medical centre

indicators.note: the picture is found inside the tube

parts.note: a hose is a flexible tube
pic is short for picture, an image

explanation.surface: A scan taken through an endoscope reveals a medical facility, or a poster on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Tube' look like the London Underground, but it is just a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospice is a care home for the terminally ill, a kind of medical institution.

clue.text: Bad weather conditions currently occurring on board to naval fighter

indicators.note: being on board a ship puts you inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel on whose board people travel
now means happening at present
RM stands for Royal Marine, a soldier serving with the navy

explanation.surface: Storms happening now, faced on deck by a sailor or marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard of falling flakes is a kind of severe winter weather.

clue.text: Praise craft shown by a lot of composition

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a work is a piece of music or writing
a ship is a sea-going craft

explanation.surface: Applauding the skill on display in most of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship is to adore or glorify, giving honour as in praising a deity.

clue.text: Crafty work, note, the first time being overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is missed out

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note worth one beat
T is short for time; only its first appearance in the note goes

explanation.surface: A cunning piece of work noted down, though at first it was missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' looks like 'sly' but means handicraft. Of the two Ts in CROTCHET, only the first is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooking yarn into fabric with a single needle is a handicraft, so it is literally work done as a craft.

clue.text: Bar very much upset about endless tirade

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the other piece
in a down entry, upset turns the word upside down so it reads upward

parts.note: most means very much, as in 'most kind'

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A pub very much in turmoil over a never-ending tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses MOST to TSOM, which goes 'about' RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door or across a window.

clue.text: Take care of half the damage in game with wife

definitions.text: Take care of half the damage

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game
dutch is Cockney slang for a wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: Accepting half the blame for something broken during a game with your wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damage' is the informal word for a bill ('what's the damage?'). DUTCH (from duchess) is London Cockney slang for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying your own share of a bill, splitting the cost equally, is the idiom for covering half.

clue.text: Lyricist, good one, boy singer mostly picked up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down entry, picked up means lifted, so the letters read upward
the last letter is left off

parts.note: a treble is a boy soprano

explanation.surface: A songwriter praising a good boy chorister lifted into the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: TREBL reversed gives LBERT. 'picked up' looks like a sound clue but is a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: W S Gilbert wrote the words for the Savoy operas with Sullivan, making him a famous librettist.

clue.text: Succeeded in blocking item at auction? Failed

indicators.note: the letter sits inside, blocking the middle of the word

parts.note: a lot is one numbered item in an auction
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees and lists of monarchs

explanation.surface: A bidder thought they had won the item at auction, but missed out.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been beaten or to have come off worse is a synonym of having failed.

clue.text: A good time you'd expect to roll?

definitions.meaning: having a ... means having a great time
a round object rolls when pushed

explanation.definitionFit: Both a lively party and a round plaything share the word: the first sense is a dance or great fun, the second a sphere.

clue.text: Player walking with difficulty by end of tour

parts.note: game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg

indicators.note: only the last letter of tour is used

explanation.surface: A sportsman limping by the final stage of a long tour.
explanation.walkthrough: GAME for lame (a game leg) is old-fashioned but still in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays video or role-playing games is a player of those games.

clue.text: Information outlets raised point about newspaperman

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the newspaperman
in a down entry, raised means read upward

parts.note: to aim is to point
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: News outlets raise a point about a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The press and broadcasters collectively are the channels of mass communication.

clue.text: Tax cut reversed after husband invested — it sounds like a blow

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, as one is clothed or installed
the shortened word is read backwards
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a duty is a tax

explanation.surface: A tax cut was reversed after a husband invested money.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull heavy sound is the noise made by a strike or fall, the noise of a blow.

clue.text: Something of horn: hard, bonelike item

parts.note: a toot is the sound a horn makes
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Describing animal horn as a hard substance resembling bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horn' suggests the material of horns, but it is the car or musical horn's toot.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth are hard, calcified structures in the jaw, close in nature to bone.

clue.text: Ideal sort for exercising, enhancing performance

indicators.note: exercising puts the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: The perfect type for working out, boosting athletic results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'for exercising' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroid drugs are taken by cheating athletes to boost strength, so they are performance-enhancing.

clue.text: Museum founder sad at a museum folding, beginning to despair

indicators.note: a business that folds collapses, and the letters collapse into a new order
only the first letter of despair is used

explanation.surface: A founder saddened as the museum closes down, starting to despair.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives MADAMETUSSAU and the D of despair completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Tussaud founded the London waxworks museum that still carries her title.
